Your starting guide

Why study
in Italy?

A new place to learn.
A future worth planning carefully.

Italy offers English-taught degrees, different types of universities and opportunities to apply for financial support. Start here to understand the benefits, the costs and what you need to prepare.

The short answer

Italy could suit your plans.
Here is what to look at first.

A suitable degree, a workable budget and a study experience that helps you grow.

Italy is worth exploring if you want an English-taught degree, a choice of university settings and funding opportunities for eligible students.

Italy has a long university tradition and study options across science, technology, business, medicine, architecture and the arts. Your experience will depend on the particular course, university and city you choose.

Compare what you will actually study, how you will be assessed and what support is available. A famous university name is useful context; it does not replace checking whether the course fits you.

For parents: look at the full plan together—academic requirements, total spending, accommodation and who will help if your child needs support.
Explore Italy’s official study introduction ↗

A choice of academic paths

Explore your subject at the right degree level. Read the course syllabus—the list of subjects and topics you will study.

Options taught in English

You can look for an English-taught course or a separate English curriculum. Availability differs by subject and study level.

Funding for eligible students

Regional and university funding may help eligible students. Check the conditions before treating an award as part of your budget.

Experience beyond the classroom

Living abroad gives you opportunities to learn a language, meet people and practise managing daily life independently.

Understand your study options

Which degree comes next for you?

You do not need to know the Italian degree names before you start. Here are the main routes we help students explore.

After Class 12

Bachelor’s
degree

Usually 3 years · Italian name: Laurea

Your first university degree after school. Choose a subject that matches your interests and previous studies.

Check first: school qualification, required subjects, English evidence and any entrance test.

After a bachelor’s degree

Master’s
degree

Usually 2 years · Laurea Magistrale

An advanced academic degree. Your previous degree and the subjects you studied must suit the programme.

Check first: academic background, subject prerequisites and course-specific selection.

A longer first degree

Medicine &
single-cycle study

Medicine: 6 years · Other routes vary

A single-cycle degree combines study into one longer programme. Medicine is one example; it is not a three-year bachelor’s followed by a separate master’s.

Check first: admission procedure, teaching language and practical-training requirements.

Choose the English-taught route.

Check the language of your exact programme or curriculum. English evidence and any Italian requirements come from the university. Learning everyday Italian will also help with shopping, appointments and settling in.

Check degree routes and entry requirements on Universitaly ↗

Fees, living costs & funding

Build a budget.
Then explore scholarships.

Italy may offer a workable study route for your family. Compare the full cost before making a decision, including the money you will need before any funding arrives.

What you need to pay for

Tuition is only one part.

There is no single fee that applies to every international student. The university, programme and applicable fee category matter.

  • University costs: tuition, application charges and any other required fees.
  • Daily living: rent, bills, food, transport and personal spending.
  • Getting started: travel, housing deposit, documents and other arrival expenses.
  • A reserve: money for unexpected costs or a delay in planned support.
See how one university explains its fee categories ↗
What may help

Two funding routes to understand.

Regional study support

Often described as DSU, regional support has financial and study-progress conditions. The responsible agency, documents, benefits and deadlines depend on where and when you study.

University scholarships

Universities may offer their own awards, including merit-based funding. Read who can apply, how selection works and what the award actually covers.

Explore regional and university funding on Universitaly ↗
Keep three things separate: admission, a scholarship and your visa. An offer of admission does not automatically include funding or a visa. Scholarship support may include services as well as money; read the relevant award conditions. Plan the funds you need at the start instead of relying on an unconfirmed scholarship or future part-time job.

Choose your everyday surroundings

The right city starts
with the right course.

Your campus, accommodation and daily journey will shape your experience as much as the city’s name.

Compare the life you would actually live.

You might explore Milan, Bologna, Rome, Pavia or another university city. First confirm which campus teaches your course—one university can have programmes in different locations.

  • Can you find housing within your budget?
  • How far is it from the teaching campus?
  • What transport and student services will you use?
  • Would you prefer a busy city or a more compact daily routine?
Ask about the accommodation process early. A university place and a room are separate arrangements. Check options, deposits and actual availability before making travel plans.
Include Pavia in your comparison. Check its courses, campus and accommodation options alongside those in other cities. Compare the same essentials for each choice so you can see which daily routine would suit you.

A clear view before you decide

What should you
be ready for?

Italy can be a good choice when you are prepared for both university study and the responsibilities of living abroad.

Take more time to plan if your budget depends entirely on a scholarship, you have not checked the course requirements, or you expect work to cover all your costs.

Managing your studies independently

You will need to follow timetables, prepare for assessments and ask for help when you need it. Compare the teaching and assessment methods before choosing.

Learning everyday Italian

Your degree may be taught in English, while much of daily life happens in Italian. Start learning useful words and phrases before you travel.

Following more than one application process

University admission, funding, accommodation and immigration steps can have different documents and deadlines. Keep one checklist with dates and submission receipts.

Building your career gradually

A degree is one part of your career plan. Language, skills and experience matter too. Look at the university’s actual career support and course opportunities; a place on a course does not promise a job.

You do not have to work out everything today

Start with three simple steps.

If you are in Class 11 or 12, begin with your subjects and interests. If you already have a degree, begin with your academic background and the area you want to study next.

  1. Write down your starting point.

    Note your current qualification, subjects, marks, English preparation, preferred start year and family budget.

  2. Compare suitable courses.

    Read the entry requirements and course subjects. Check the teaching language and campus before making a shortlist.

  3. Build your application plan.

    List the documents, tests, application dates and funding deadlines for each option. Then plan housing and the steps after admission.

What will we check when discussing your eligibility?

Your school or university qualification, relevant subjects, academic results, language evidence and the requirements of your shortlisted course. Meeting a basic requirement is different from being selected for admission.

Read the official application starting guide ↗ or discuss your starting point with EuroMiles ↓

Questions students & parents ask

A few things
made simpler.

Tap a question to read the answer.

Can I study in Italy after Class 12?
You can explore bachelor’s and suitable single-cycle programmes after school. The university checks your qualification and the course’s subject, language and selection requirements. Start with those checks rather than assuming Class 12 alone guarantees eligibility.
Can I study in English without knowing Italian?
Look for a programme or curriculum taught in English, then check its language conditions. Some courses have additional requirements for practical or clinical activities. Everyday Italian will still help you settle in, even when your classes are in English.
Is studying in Italy completely free?
Do not assume that. Tuition reductions and scholarships have conditions, and you still need a plan for living and initial expenses. Compare your actual fee category and the award rules instead of relying on a general “free education” claim.
Does admission mean I will get a scholarship?
No. Admission and funding are separate decisions. Check whether an award requires another application, which documents it needs and when the results and benefits become available.
Should I choose a university only by its ranking?
Use rankings as one comparison point. Also check the course subjects, entry requirements, teaching language, campus, costs and support. The course must fit your goals and previous studies.
Can a student job pay for everything?
Do not build your budget on that assumption. Finding suitable work and earning a particular amount are uncertain. Arrange reliable study funds first, and check the current conditions that apply to student work.
When should I start preparing?
Start while you still have time to improve your academic and English preparation and collect documents. Work backwards from your chosen course’s published deadlines; there is no single application date for every university and scholarship.
